"""
Widgets for playing timelines, built on feather-tk: a Viewport that draws a Player's frames, a TimelineWidget, and tool bars and time widgets for the transport. They go in a feather_tk.App window, whose loop ticks the context and draws; tlrender.ui.init() comes first.
"""

from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
import enum
from typing import overload

import feather_tk._feather_tk
import opentimelineio.opentime

import tlrender._tlrender


def init(context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> None:
    """
    Initialize the library, and tlRender's core with it: call it instead of tlrender.init() before making any of the widgets.
    """

class ItemData:
    """
    What the items of a timeline widget share: the speed, the directory relative media paths are read against, the options and the time units model. TimelineWidget makes its own; a TimelineRuler is given one.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def speed(self) -> float: ...

    @speed.setter
    def speed(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dir(self) -> str: ...

    @dir.setter
    def dir(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def options(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.Options: ...

    @options.setter
    def options(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.Options, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def timeUnitsModel(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.ITimeUnitsModel: ...

    @timeUnitsModel.setter
    def timeUnitsModel(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.ITimeUnitsModel, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def toMediaTime(self) -> Callable[[opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime], opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime]:
        """
        How to turn a time on the timeline into the time shown for it; see TimeMap. Only positions go through it, a duration being a length either way. Unset, the two are the same.
        """

    @toMediaTime.setter
    def toMediaTime(self, arg: Callable[[opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime], opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime], /) -> None: ...

class ThumbnailSystem(feather_tk._feather_tk.ISystem):
    """
    Makes the thumbnails and audio waveforms the timeline widget draws, on threads of its own, and keeps them. tlrender.ui.init() creates it. Only the cache is reached from Python.
    """

    def clearCache(self) -> None:
        """
        Clear the thumbnails and waveforms made so far, to free their memory. A file changed on disk does not need it: its modification time is part of what they are kept by, so it is read again.
        """

def setFileBrowserIOOptions(context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, options: Mapping[str, str]) -> None:
    """Set the I/O options the file browser reads its thumbnails with."""

class TimeMap:
    """
    Maps between the time a player runs on and the time shown for it, which are not always the same: a sequence read with its missing frames left out plays at the length of the frames it has, so counting from the start does not name the frame, and the media's own time does. toMedia and fromMedia are functions of a RationalTime; left unset the two times are the same.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def toMedia(self) -> Callable[[opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime], opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime]: ...

    @toMedia.setter
    def toMedia(self, arg: Callable[[opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime], opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fromMedia(self) -> Callable[[opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime], opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime]: ...

    @fromMedia.setter
    def fromMedia(self, arg: Callable[[opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime], opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime], /) -> None: ...

class TimeEdit(feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget):
    """
    Edits a time, as text in the time units model's units: frames, seconds or timecode.
    """

    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, timeUnitsModel: tlrender._tlrender.TimeUnitsModel, parent: feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None:
        """Get the time value, unset when the edit has none."""

    @value.setter
    def value(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None, /) -> None: ...

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the time value callback."""

    def setTimeMap(self, arg: TimeMap, /) -> None:
        """
        Set the mapping between the value and the time shown. The value, and the callback, stay in the player's time.
        """

    def setRange(self, range: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None) -> None:
        """
        Set the times the value can take, in the player's time, so the edit is wide enough for any of them.
        """

    def selectAll(self) -> None:
        """Select all."""

class TimelineWidget(feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget):
    """
    Draws a Player's timeline -- tracks, clips, transitions, markers, thumbnails and audio waveforms -- under a ruler that scrubs it, with the timelines the player compares against drawn beside it. Give it a player; it follows the player's time. Thumbnails and waveforms are made on other threads by the ThumbnailSystem and fill in as they arrive.
    """

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, parent: feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, timeUnitsModel: tlrender._tlrender.ITimeUnitsModel, parent: feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def timeUnitsModel(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.ITimeUnitsModel:
        """Get the time units model."""

    @property
    def player(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.Player:
        """The player whose timeline is drawn, or None."""

    @player.setter
    def player(self, value: tlrender._tlrender.Player | None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def displayOptions(self) -> DisplayOptions:
        """Get the display options."""

    @displayOptions.setter
    def displayOptions(self, arg: DisplayOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeDisplayOptions(self) -> IObservableDisplayOptions:
        """Observe the display options."""

    def setTimelines(self, timelines: Sequence[tlrender._tlrender.Timeline] | None) -> None:
        """
        Set the timelines drawn beside the player's own. None, the default, draws the player's compare timelines; a list draws those instead, for showing timelines the picture is not comparing.
        """

    @property
    def frameMarkers(self) -> list[int]:
        """Get the frame markers."""

    @frameMarkers.setter
    def frameMarkers(self, arg: Sequence[int], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def markers(self) -> list[Marker]:
        """Get the markers."""

    @markers.setter
    def markers(self, arg: Sequence[Marker], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def frameView(self) -> bool:
        """
        Whether the view is framed automatically: the whole timeline fitted to the widget's width.
        """

    @frameView.setter
    def frameView(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeFrameView(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether the view is framed automatically."""

    @property
    def scrollBarsVisible(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the scroll bars are visible."""

    @scrollBarsVisible.setter
    def scrollBarsVisible(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeScrollBarsVisible(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether the scroll bars are visible."""

    @property
    def autoScroll(self) -> bool:
        """
        Whether the view scrolls to keep the current time in view during playback.
        """

    @autoScroll.setter
    def autoScroll(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeAutoScroll(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether auto-scroll is enabled."""

    @property
    def stopOnScrub(self) -> bool:
        """Whether scrubbing stops playback."""

    @stopOnScrub.setter
    def stopOnScrub(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeStopOnScrub(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether to stop playback when scrubbing."""

class TimelineRuler(feather_tk._feather_tk.IMouseWidget):
    """
    The time ruler a TimelineWidget draws above its timelines, with the player's in and out points, frame markers and cache. TimelineWidget makes and places its own; this is for a layout of one's own, which then sets the scale and scroll position as the timelines move.
    """

    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, itemData: ItemData, parent: feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setItemData(self, arg: ItemData, /) -> None:
        """Set the item data, which the labels are named through."""

    def setPlayer(self, player: tlrender._tlrender.Player | None) -> None:
        """Set the player."""

    def setScale(self, arg: float, /) -> None:
        """Set the scale, in pixels per second."""

    def setScrollPos(self, arg: int, /) -> None:
        """Set how far the timelines are scrolled, so that the ruler is over
        the part of them it names.
        """

    def setOffset(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, /) -> None:
        """Set how far along the timeline is drawn."""

    def setFrameMarkers(self, arg: Sequence[int], /) -> None:
        """Set the frame markers."""

    def setDisplayOptions(self, arg: DisplayOptions, /) -> None:
        """Set the display options."""

    def setOptions(self, arg: ItemOptions, /) -> None:
        """Set the options."""

    def setStopOnScrub(self, arg: bool, /) -> None:
        """Set whether playback stops when scrubbing."""

    @property
    def observeScrub(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether scrubbing is in progress."""

    def timeToPos(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, /) -> int:
        """Convert a time to a position."""

class Viewport(feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget):
    """
    Draws a Player's current frames, a comparison included, with the OCIO, LUT, image and display options applied, and lets the mouse pan, zoom and wipe. Give it a player and it redraws whenever the player presents a frame. For the same picture without a window, as an image, see OffscreenRender.
    """

    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, parent: feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def compareOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.CompareOptions: ...

    @compareOptions.setter
    def compareOptions(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.CompareOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCompareOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.IObservableCompareOptions: ...

    @property
    def ocioOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.OCIOOptions: ...

    @ocioOptions.setter
    def ocioOptions(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.OCIOOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property

    @property
    def observeLUTOptions(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.IObservableLUTOptions: ...

    @property

    @property
    def player(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.Player:
        """The player whose frames are drawn, or None."""

    @player.setter
    def player(self, value: tlrender._tlrender.Player | None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def viewPos(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.V2I:
        """Get the view position."""

    @property
    def observeViewPos(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableV2I:
        """Observe the view position."""

    @property
    def zoom(self) -> float:
        """Get the view zoom."""

    def observeZoom(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableDouble:
        """Observe the view zoom."""

    @property
    def viewPosAndZoom(self) -> tuple[feather_tk._feather_tk.V2I, float]:
        """Get the view position and zoom."""

        """Set the view position and zoom."""

    @property
    def observeViewPosAndZoom(self) -> IObservableViewPosAndZoom:
        """Observe the view position and zoom."""

    def setZoom(self, zoom: float, focus: feather_tk._feather_tk.V2I = ...) -> None:
        """Set the view zoom."""

    @overload
    def center(self) -> None:
        """Center the view."""

    @overload
    def center(self) -> None:
        """Center the view."""

    @overload
    def resetZoom(self) -> None:
        """Reset the view zoom to 1:1."""

    @overload
    def resetZoom(self) -> None:
        """Reset the view zoom to 1:1."""

    @overload
    def zoomIn(self) -> None:
        """Zoom the view in."""

    @overload
    def zoomIn(self) -> None:
        """Zoom the view in."""

        """Zoom the view out."""

        """Zoom the view out."""

    @property

        """Get the view zoom range."""

    def zoomRange(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.RangeD, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def frameView(self) -> bool:
        """
        Whether the view is framed automatically: the picture fitted to the viewport, again as either changes size.
        """

    @frameView.setter
    def frameView(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeFrameView(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether the view is framed automatically."""

    @property
    def observeFramed(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe when the view is framed."""

    @property
    def FPS(self) -> float:
        """
        The frames per second the player presents while it plays, measured about once a second; zero when stopped. In an App, where each tick also draws, that is the rate frames are shown. A script that calls Context.tick() more often than it draws measures the frames presented, not the frames drawn.
        """

    @property
    def observeFPS(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableDouble:
        """Observe the frames per second."""

    @property
    def droppedFrames(self) -> int:
        """
        The player's dropped frames: see Player.droppedFrames. Frames the player presented that were never drawn are not counted; in an App they cannot happen, since the player presents at most one frame between draws.
        """

    @property
    def observeDroppedFrames(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableSizeT:
        """Observe the number of dropped frames during playback."""

    def getColorSample(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.V2I, /) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """
        Sample a color, at a position in the viewport's own coordinates. It is read back from the buffer the viewport drew into, so it is the frame before the one being drawn, and the read waits for the GPU: sampling every frame stalls the playback being sampled.
        """

    def getColorSampleDisplay(self, color: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """Get the color a sample is shown as in the window. It is the sample
        itself but for a PQ picture drawn with the GPU renderer, which is taken
        into what the window holds as it is drawn there.
        """

    def getColorSampleNits(self, color: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F) -> float | None:
        """Get the luminance, in nits, that a sample stands for: what a PQ
        picture's code values say, or what an HDR window makes of an SDR
        picture. Unset where nothing says, which is an SDR picture in an SDR
        window.
        """

    @property
    def hdrTransfer(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.HDR_EOTF:
        """Get what the picture is display encoded for."""

    @hdrTransfer.setter
    def hdrTransfer(self, arg: tlrender._tlrender.HDR_EOTF, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hdrWhite(self) -> float:
        """Get the luminance that white in the window stands for."""

    @hdrWhite.setter
    def hdrWhite(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeSamplePos(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableV2I:
        """Observe the sample position, in the viewport's own coordinates."""

    @property
    def observePick(self) -> IObservableOptionalV2I:
        """Observe picking. Unset when the position is not over an image, where
        there is no pixel to name.
        """

    @property
    def observeColorSample(self) -> IObservableOptionalColor4F:
        """Observe the color sample. Unset when the position is not over an
        image.
        """

    def pick(self, imagePos: feather_tk._feather_tk.V2I) -> None:
        """
        Sample the image at an image pixel, as the pick mouse action would; the result arrives through observeColorSample.
        """

    @property
    def inputEnabled(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether input is enabled."""

    @inputEnabled.setter
    def inputEnabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def setPanBinding(self, button: feather_tk._feather_tk.MouseButton, modifier: feather_tk._feather_tk.KeyModifier) -> None:
        """Set the pan binding."""

    def setWipeBinding(self, button: feather_tk._feather_tk.MouseButton, modifier: feather_tk._feather_tk.KeyModifier) -> None:
        """Set the wipe binding."""

    def setPickBinding(self, button: feather_tk._feather_tk.MouseButton, modifier: feather_tk._feather_tk.KeyModifier) -> None:
        """Set the pick binding. Unbound by default."""

    def setMouseWheelScale(self, arg: float, /) -> None:
        """Set the mouse wheel scale."""
